note: Draft layer written by Claude on 2026-10-25 where Wikidata and Pantheon are thin; each row names the Wikipedia article it was written from. Waiting for the judge.

rows.name: First Battle of Panipat
rows.desc: Babur defeated Sultan Ibrahim Lodi with field guns and cavalry tactics, ending the Delhi Sultanate.

rows.name: Death of Ibrahim Lodi
rows.desc: The last Lodi sultan of Delhi was killed on the field at Panipat.

rows.name: Babur rules from Agra
rows.desc: Babur, founder of the Mughal dynasty, made Agra his seat after Panipat.

rows.name: Humayun receives the Koh-i-Noor at Agra
rows.desc: The family of the Raja of Gwalior gave Humayun a great diamond, usually identified with the Koh-i-Noor, after Panipat.

rows.name: Aram Bagh laid out
rows.desc: Babur laid out a riverside charbagh garden at Agra, among the oldest Mughal gardens in India.

rows.name: Kabuli Bagh mosque at Panipat
rows.desc: Babur built a mosque and garden at Panipat to mark his victory.

rows.name: Battle of Khanwa
rows.desc: Babur defeated Rana Sanga of Mewar and his Rajput and Afghan allies near Fatehpur Sikri.

rows.name: Baburnama
rows.desc: Babur's Chagatai Turkic memoir describes Hindustan's fruits, towns and customs as he found them.

rows.name: Death of Babur
rows.desc: Babur died at Agra and was first buried in a garden there before removal to Kabul.

rows.name: Humayun on the throne at Agra
rows.desc: Humayun succeeded Babur and ruled from Agra and Delhi until driven out by Sher Shah.

rows.name: Humayun founds Dinpanah
rows.desc: Humayun began a new city called Dinpanah on the old mound of Indraprastha at Delhi.

rows.name: Jamali Kamali mosque
rows.desc: A mosque and tomb built in Mehrauli for the Sufi poet Jamali, completed about 1535.

rows.name: Sher Shah Suri holds Delhi and Agra
rows.desc: The Afghan ruler Sher Shah expelled Humayun and governed from Agra and Delhi, reforming revenue, roads and coinage.

rows.name: Silver rupiya issued
rows.desc: Sher Shah's government struck a standard silver coin, the rupiya, ancestor of the rupee.

rows.name: Grand Trunk Road and its sarais
rows.desc: Sher Shah rebuilt the great road through Delhi and Agra with sarais and wells at regular stages.

rows.name: Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque
rows.desc: Sher Shah's congregational mosque inside the Purana Qila, a high point of Afghan architecture.

rows.name: Sher Mandal
rows.desc: An octagonal two-storey tower in the Purana Qila, later used by Humayun as his library.

rows.name: Islam Shah Suri rules
rows.desc: Sher Shah's son Islam Shah ruled the Suri state from 1545 to 1554.

rows.name: Salimgarh Fort
rows.desc: Islam Shah Suri built a fort on an island of the Yamuna at Delhi.

rows.name: Tomb of Isa Khan
rows.desc: The octagonal tomb of the Suri noble Isa Khan Niazi was built near the dargah of Nizamuddin.

rows.name: Famine around Agra and Delhi
rows.desc: Chroniclers including Badayuni described famine and pestilence in the Agra and Delhi region during the wars of 1555 to 1556.

rows.name: Humayun retakes Delhi
rows.desc: After victory at Sirhind, Humayun reoccupied Delhi and restored Mughal rule.

rows.name: Death of Humayun
rows.desc: Humayun died days after falling on the stairs of the Sher Mandal library.

rows.name: Battle of Delhi (1556)
rows.desc: Hemu defeated the Mughal governor Tardi Beg Khan at Tughlaqabad and took Delhi.

rows.name: Hemu proclaimed Vikramaditya
rows.desc: Hemu assumed royal status in Delhi under the title Raja Vikramaditya.

rows.name: Second Battle of Panipat
rows.desc: Akbar's army under Bairam Khan defeated Hemu, who was struck in the eye by an arrow and captured.

rows.name: Death of Hemu
rows.desc: Hemu was beheaded after his capture at Panipat.

rows.name: Bairam Khan regent
rows.desc: Bairam Khan governed the empire as regent for the young Akbar.

rows.name: Akbar reigns
rows.desc: Akbar ruled from Agra, Fatehpur Sikri and later Lahore, building the Mughal state.

rows.name: Court settles at Agra
rows.desc: Akbar moved his court to Agra, which became the main Mughal capital.

rows.name: Fall of Bairam Khan
rows.desc: Akbar dismissed his regent and began to rule in his own name.

rows.name: Khair-ul-Manazil
rows.desc: The wet nurse Maham Anga built a mosque and madrasa facing the Purana Qila.

rows.name: Adham Khan thrown from the ramparts
rows.desc: Akbar had his foster brother Adham Khan thrown from a terrace after he murdered the minister Ataga Khan.

rows.name: Adham Khan's tomb
rows.desc: An octagonal tomb in Mehrauli for Adham Khan and his mother Maham Anga.

rows.name: Tansen at court
rows.desc: The singer Tansen joined Akbar's court and became one of its Nine Jewels.

rows.name: Hamzanama
rows.desc: Akbar's studio painted about 1,400 large pictures of the Hamza romance, roughly 1562 to 1577.

rows.name: Mir Sayyid Ali heads the studio
rows.desc: The Persian master Mir Sayyid Ali supervised the Hamzanama in Akbar's workshop.

rows.name: Abd al-Samad at the imperial studio
rows.desc: The Persian painter Abd al-Samad led the imperial workshop after Mir Sayyid Ali.

rows.name: Jizya abolished
rows.desc: Akbar abolished the poll tax on non-Muslims.

rows.name: Agra Fort rebuilt
rows.desc: Akbar began rebuilding Agra Fort in red sandstone, work completed about 1573.

rows.name: Humayun's Tomb begun
rows.desc: Bega Begum commissioned Humayun's garden tomb, designed by Mirak Mirza Ghiyas and finished about 1572.

rows.name: Mirak Mirza Ghiyas
rows.desc: The Persian architect designed Humayun's Tomb.

rows.name: Tomb of Ataga Khan
rows.desc: A marble inlaid tomb for the minister Ataga Khan at Nizamuddin.

rows.name: Arab ki Sarai
rows.desc: A walled sarai near Humayun's Tomb, traditionally linked to Persian craftsmen working on the tomb.

rows.name: Birth of Prince Salim
rows.desc: The future Jahangir was born at Sikri, in the hermitage of Shaikh Salim Chishti.

rows.name: Birth of Prince Murad
rows.desc: Akbar's second son Murad was born at Fatehpur Sikri.

rows.name: Fatehpur Sikri founded
rows.desc: Akbar built a new capital at Sikri to honour Shaikh Salim Chishti.

rows.name: Jama Masjid, Fatehpur Sikri
rows.desc: The great congregational mosque of Akbar's new capital, completed about 1572.

rows.name: Death of Shaikh Salim Chishti
rows.desc: The Sufi saint whose blessing Akbar credited for his sons died at Sikri.

rows.name: Buland Darwaza
rows.desc: A towering gateway was added to the Fatehpur Sikri mosque after the conquest of Gujarat.

rows.name: Tomb of Salim Chishti
rows.desc: A white marble tomb with carved screens was raised in the mosque courtyard.

rows.name: Panch Mahal
rows.desc: A five-storey open pavilion in the palace complex of Fatehpur Sikri.

rows.name: Ibadat Khana
rows.desc: Akbar built a house of worship for debates among Muslim, Hindu, Jain, Zoroastrian and Christian scholars.

rows.name: Mansabdari and branding of horses
rows.desc: Akbar graded officers by numerical rank and required branding of cavalry horses.

rows.name: Todar Mal
rows.desc: Raja Todar Mal reorganised land revenue assessment for Akbar.

rows.name: Dahsala revenue system
rows.desc: A ten-year average of yields and prices fixed cash revenue demands in the core provinces.

rows.name: Birbal
rows.desc: Raja Birbal was a close companion and wit at Akbar's court.

rows.name: Abd al-Qadir Badayuni
rows.desc: The orthodox scholar served at court and later wrote a critical history of Akbar's reign.

rows.name: Birth of Faizi
rows.desc: Faizi, later Akbar's poet laureate, was born at Agra.

rows.name: Birth of Abul Fazl
rows.desc: Abul Fazl, Akbar's vizier and historian, was born at Agra.

rows.name: Abul Fazl at court
rows.desc: Abul Fazl entered Akbar's service and became his chief ideologue and chronicler.

rows.name: Mahzar declaration
rows.desc: Leading ulama signed a decree recognising Akbar as final arbiter in disputed religious questions.

rows.name: First Jesuit mission arrives
rows.desc: Rudolf Acquaviva and Antoni de Montserrat reached Fatehpur Sikri from Goa.

rows.name: Antoni de Montserrat
rows.desc: The Catalan Jesuit tutored Prince Murad and wrote an account of Akbar's court.

rows.name: Din-i Ilahi
rows.desc: Akbar formed a circle of disciples around an eclectic creed later called Din-i Ilahi.

rows.name: Razmnama
rows.desc: The Persian translation of the Mahabharata was made and illustrated at Fatehpur Sikri, about 1582 to 1586.

rows.name: Daswanth
rows.desc: A painter of humble birth who became a leading artist of the Razmnama.

rows.name: Basawan
rows.desc: A leading painter of Akbar's studio known for portraiture and depth.

rows.name: Tarikh-i Ilahi calendar
rows.desc: Akbar introduced a solar era dated from his accession.

rows.name: Court leaves Fatehpur Sikri
rows.desc: Akbar moved north to Lahore, and Fatehpur Sikri lost its role as capital.

rows.name: Ralph Fitch
rows.desc: The English merchant visited Agra and Fatehpur Sikri and judged each larger than London.

rows.name: Persian Baburnama
rows.desc: Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khanan translated Babur's memoir into Persian for Akbar.

rows.name: Akbarnama begun
rows.desc: Abul Fazl began the official history of Akbar's reign, with the Ain-i-Akbari as its last part.

rows.name: Ain-i-Akbari
rows.desc: The administrative account of Akbar's empire, covering revenue, prices, wages and crafts.

rows.name: Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh
rows.desc: Badayuni completed his secret, critical history of the reign.

rows.name: Govind Dev temple
rows.desc: Raja Man Singh of Amber built a great red sandstone temple to Krishna at Vrindavan.

rows.name: Jal Mahal, Narnaul
rows.desc: The governor Shah Quli Khan built a pavilion in a tank at Narnaul.

rows.name: Famine of 1595 to 1598
rows.desc: A long famine struck northern India, with heavy mortality reported around Agra and Lahore.

rows.name: Court returns to Agra
rows.desc: Akbar returned from Lahore and made Agra his capital again.

rows.name: Tomb of Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khanan
rows.desc: Khan-i-Khanan built a tomb for his wife, where he too was later buried.

rows.name: Akbar's Church
rows.desc: Jesuits built a chapel at Agra on land granted by Akbar.

rows.name: Jerome Xavier
rows.desc: The Navarrese Jesuit led the third mission to Akbar and Jahangir and wrote Persian works on Christianity.

rows.name: Bento de Gois sets out for Cathay
rows.desc: The Jesuit lay brother left Agra to seek a land route to China.

rows.name: Death of Akbar
rows.desc: Akbar died at Agra Fort.

rows.name: Akbar's tomb
rows.desc: Akbar's tomb at Sikandra was begun and completed by Jahangir about 1613.

rows.name: Jahangir reigns
rows.desc: Jahangir succeeded at Agra and ruled until 1627.

rows.name: Chain of Justice
rows.desc: Jahangir hung a golden chain with bells so petitioners could appeal to him directly.

rows.name: Khusrau flees Agra
rows.desc: Prince Khusrau escaped from Agra Fort and rose in rebellion against his father.

rows.name: Faridabad founded
rows.desc: Shaikh Farid, treasurer of Jahangir, founded a town to guard the highway south of Delhi.

rows.name: William Hawkins at Agra
rows.desc: The English captain sought trading rights at Jahangir's court and stayed about two years.

rows.name: Jahangir marries Nur Jahan
rows.desc: Jahangir married Mehr-un-Nissa, titled Nur Jahan, who became the most powerful woman in the empire.

rows.name: Nur Jahan
rows.desc: Nur Jahan issued coins and orders and patronised building and trade.

rows.name: Itimad-ud-Daulah
rows.desc: Mirza Ghiyas Beg, Nur Jahan's father, served as chief minister.

rows.name: Death of John Mildenhall
rows.desc: The English adventurer died at Agra, among the earliest English burials in India.

rows.name: Thomas Coryat
rows.desc: The English walker visited Agra and the Mughal court on foot from Europe.

rows.name: Plague in northern India
rows.desc: Jahangir recorded a plague that spread from the Punjab to Agra over several years.

rows.name: Abu al-Hasan
rows.desc: Jahangir's favourite painter, titled Nadir al-Zaman.

rows.name: Ustad Mansur
rows.desc: Jahangir's painter of birds, animals and flowers.

rows.name: Jahangirnama
rows.desc: Jahangir wrote his own memoirs, noting natural history, justice and court life.

rows.name: Keshava Deva temple, Mathura
rows.desc: Bir Singh Deo Bundela built a large temple at Krishna's birthplace in Mathura.

rows.name: Francisco Pelsaert
rows.desc: The Dutch factor at Agra wrote a sharp account of Mughal trade and the poverty of workers.

rows.name: Indigo of Bayana
rows.desc: European companies bought indigo at Bayana, the most prized in northern India.

rows.name: Remonstrantie
rows.desc: Pelsaert's report described prices, wages, crafts and markets of Agra.

rows.name: Death of Mariam-uz-Zamani
rows.desc: Akbar's Rajput queen and Jahangir's mother died at Agra.

rows.name: Tomb of Mariam-uz-Zamani
rows.desc: Jahangir built a tomb for his mother at Sikandra.

rows.name: Chausath Khamba
rows.desc: A marble hall of sixty-four pillars built as the tomb of Mirza Aziz Koka.

rows.name: Tomb of I'timad-ud-Daulah
rows.desc: Nur Jahan built a marble tomb with inlay for her parents, completed about 1628.

rows.name: Birth of Mumtaz Mahal
rows.desc: Arjumand Banu Begum, later Mumtaz Mahal, was born at Agra.

rows.name: Death of Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khanan
rows.desc: The general, poet and translator died at Delhi.

rows.name: Shah Jahan enthroned
rows.desc: Shah Jahan was proclaimed emperor at Agra.

rows.name: Shah Jahan reigns
rows.desc: Shah Jahan ruled from Agra and from 1648 from Delhi until deposed in 1658.

rows.name: Peter Mundy at Agra
rows.desc: The English factor recorded the building of the Taj and daily life in Agra.

rows.name: Taj Mahal begun
rows.desc: Shah Jahan began a marble mausoleum for Mumtaz Mahal on the Yamuna, finished about 1653.

rows.name: Ustad Ahmad Lahori
rows.desc: The architect traditionally credited with designing the Taj Mahal and the Red Fort.

rows.name: Taj Ganj bazaar
rows.desc: A walled quarter of markets and sarais was built south of the Taj to fund its upkeep.

rows.name: Peacock Throne unveiled
rows.desc: The jewelled Peacock Throne was first used at Agra.

rows.name: Chini ka Rauza
rows.desc: A glazed tile tomb for the poet and minister Afzal Khan Shirazi.

rows.name: Khas Mahal, Agra Fort
rows.desc: Shah Jahan rebuilt the private palace in white marble.

rows.name: Padshahnama
rows.desc: Abdul Hamid Lahori wrote the official history of Shah Jahan's reign, with illustrated copies.

rows.name: Bichitr
rows.desc: Mughal painter of allegorical portraits of Jahangir and Shah Jahan.

rows.name: Chandar Bhan Brahman
rows.desc: The Hindu Persian poet served as secretary under Shah Jahan.

rows.name: Tavernier
rows.desc: The French jewel merchant visited Agra on the first of several journeys.

rows.name: Shahjahanabad founded
rows.desc: Shah Jahan began a new walled capital at Delhi.

rows.name: Red Fort begun
rows.desc: The palace fortress of Shahjahanabad was begun, and Shah Jahan entered it in 1648.

rows.name: Canal brought to Delhi
rows.desc: Ali Mardan Khan renewed an old canal to carry Yamuna water into Shahjahanabad.

rows.name: Ardhakathanak
rows.desc: The Jain merchant Banarasidas finished his verse autobiography at Agra, the first in an Indian language.

rows.name: Banarasidas
rows.desc: The Jain merchant poet lived and traded in Agra.

rows.name: Court moves to Delhi
rows.desc: Shah Jahan formally entered the Red Fort, making Shahjahanabad the capital.

rows.name: Jama Masjid, Agra
rows.desc: Jahanara Begum funded a congregational mosque by Agra Fort.

rows.name: Moti Masjid, Agra
rows.desc: A white marble mosque inside Agra Fort, completed about 1654.

rows.name: Jahanara Begum
rows.desc: Shah Jahan's eldest daughter held the title Padshah Begum and patronised buildings and trade.

rows.name: Chandni Chowk
rows.desc: Jahanara planned the moonlit market street with a canal down its centre.

rows.name: Jahanara's caravanserai
rows.desc: Jahanara built a large sarai on Chandni Chowk for travelling merchants.

rows.name: Fatehpuri Masjid
rows.desc: A queen of Shah Jahan built a mosque at the west end of Chandni Chowk.

rows.name: Jama Masjid, Delhi
rows.desc: The largest Mughal mosque was built at Shahjahanabad, completed in 1656.

rows.name: Roshanara Bagh
rows.desc: Princess Roshanara laid out a garden north of the city.

rows.name: Shalimar Bagh, Delhi
rows.desc: A royal garden north of Delhi, later the site of Aurangzeb's first coronation.

rows.name: Leaks reported at the Taj
rows.desc: Prince Aurangzeb wrote that the Taj dome leaked and the Mehtab Bagh had flooded.

rows.name: Mehtab Bagh
rows.desc: The moonlight garden opposite the Taj was aligned with the mausoleum.

rows.name: Shikohabad
rows.desc: A town named after Prince Dara Shikoh.

rows.name: Dara Shikoh
rows.desc: Shah Jahan's heir and a scholar of Sufism and Vedanta.

rows.name: Majma-ul-Bahrain
rows.desc: Dara Shikoh compared Sufi and Vedantic ideas in The Confluence of the Two Seas.

rows.name: Sirr-i-Akbar
rows.desc: Dara Shikoh had fifty Upanishads translated into Persian at Delhi.

rows.name: Niccolao Manucci
rows.desc: The Venetian adventurer served Dara Shikoh as gunner and later wrote Storia do Mogor.

rows.name: Shah Jahan falls ill
rows.desc: The emperor's illness at Delhi set off rumours of his death and the princes' war.

rows.name: Battle of Samugarh
rows.desc: Aurangzeb and Murad defeated Dara Shikoh east of Agra.

rows.name: Siege of Agra Fort
rows.desc: Aurangzeb cut the water supply and forced Shah Jahan to surrender the fort.

rows.name: Shah Jahan confined
rows.desc: The deposed emperor was held in Agra Fort until his death.

rows.name: Aurangzeb crowned at Shalimar Bagh
rows.desc: Aurangzeb was first crowned in the Shalimar garden outside Delhi.

rows.name: Murad Bakhsh imprisoned
rows.desc: Aurangzeb seized Murad Bakhsh and held him at Salimgarh before Gwalior.

rows.name: Aurangzeb reigns
rows.desc: Aurangzeb ruled from Delhi until he left for the Deccan in 1679.

rows.name: Francois Bernier
rows.desc: The French physician lived in Delhi under Danishmand Khan and described the city.

rows.name: Dara paraded through Delhi
rows.desc: The captured Dara Shikoh was paraded on a mean elephant through Chandni Chowk, as Bernier witnessed.

rows.name: Execution of Dara Shikoh
rows.desc: Dara Shikoh was executed and buried in Humayun's Tomb.

rows.name: Moti Masjid, Red Fort
rows.desc: Aurangzeb built a small marble mosque inside the Red Fort.

rows.name: Execution of Sarmad Kashani
rows.desc: The Armenian-Jewish Sufi poet close to Dara was executed near the Jama Masjid.

rows.name: Death of Guru Har Krishan
rows.desc: The eighth Sikh guru died of smallpox in Delhi while tending the sick.

rows.name: Smallpox in Delhi
rows.desc: A smallpox epidemic struck Delhi.

rows.name: Gurdwara Bangla Sahib
rows.desc: The bungalow where Guru Har Krishan stayed became a Sikh shrine.

rows.name: Tavernier sees the Peacock Throne
rows.desc: Tavernier described the Peacock Throne and Aurangzeb's jewels at Delhi.

rows.name: Death of Shah Jahan
rows.desc: Shah Jahan died in Agra Fort and was buried beside Mumtaz Mahal.

rows.name: Shivaji at the Agra court
rows.desc: Shivaji attended Aurangzeb's birthday court at Agra and was placed under house arrest.

rows.name: Shivaji escapes from Agra
rows.desc: Shivaji escaped house arrest, reputedly hidden in sweet baskets.

rows.name: Ram Singh I
rows.desc: The Kachhwaha prince guarded Shivaji at Agra and lost favour after the escape.

rows.name: Gokula's Jat rising
rows.desc: Jat peasants under Gokula killed the faujdar of Mathura and fought Mughal troops at Tilpat.

rows.name: Execution of Gokula
rows.desc: Gokula was executed at Agra after his capture.

rows.name: Keshava Deva temple destroyed
rows.desc: On Aurangzeb's orders the great Mathura temple was demolished and a mosque raised on the site.

rows.name: Shrinathji leaves Govardhan
rows.desc: Priests carried the image of Shrinathji from Govardhan, reaching Nathdwara in Mewar by 1672.

rows.name: Fatawa-e-Alamgiri
rows.desc: A board of jurists compiled a digest of Hanafi law for Aurangzeb, about 1667 to 1675.

rows.name: Travels in the Mogul Empire
rows.desc: Bernier's account of Mughal Delhi and the court was published in Paris.

rows.name: Death of Roshanara Begum
rows.desc: Aurangzeb's sister and ally died at Delhi.

rows.name: Satnami revolt
rows.desc: The Satnami sect rose near Narnaul after a quarrel with a soldier and was crushed by imperial troops.

rows.name: Execution of Guru Tegh Bahadur
rows.desc: The ninth Sikh guru was beheaded at Chandni Chowk on Aurangzeb's orders.

rows.name: Gurdwara Sis Ganj Sahib
rows.desc: A Sikh shrine later marked the site of the guru's execution.

rows.name: Guru's body cremated at Rakab Ganj
rows.desc: Lakhi Shah Vanjara cremated the guru's body by burning his own house.

rows.name: Jizya reimposed
rows.desc: Aurangzeb restored the poll tax on non-Muslims, provoking protests in Delhi.

rows.name: Aurangzeb leaves for the Deccan
rows.desc: Aurangzeb left north India for Rajasthan and the Deccan and never returned to Delhi.

rows.name: Death of Jahanara Begum
rows.desc: Jahanara died at Delhi and was buried in an open grave at Nizamuddin.

rows.name: Rajaram Jat
rows.desc: Rajaram of Sinsini organised Jat resistance around Agra.

rows.name: Jats plunder Akbar's tomb
rows.desc: Jat rebels under Rajaram plundered Akbar's tomb at Sikandra.

rows.name: Fall of Sinsini
rows.desc: Mughal forces under Bishan Singh of Amber captured the Jat stronghold of Sinsini.

rows.name: Churaman
rows.desc: Churaman led the Jats and built strongholds such as Thun.

rows.name: Death of Zeb-un-Nissa
rows.desc: Aurangzeb's poet daughter died at Delhi while confined in Salimgarh.

rows.name: Zinat-ul-Masajid
rows.desc: Aurangzeb's daughter Zinat-un-Nissa built a riverside mosque in Daryaganj.

rows.name: Battle of Jajau
rows.desc: Prince Muazzam defeated and killed his brother Azam Shah and became Bahadur Shah I.

rows.name: Kos minars
rows.desc: Mughal pillars marked each kos along the highway between Agra, Delhi and Lahore.

rows.name: Shah Pir's tomb, Meerut
rows.desc: A red sandstone tomb was built at Meerut for the Sufi Shah Pir.

rows.name: Agra the great mart
rows.desc: Agra was the chief market of the empire for indigo, cotton cloth and overland trade.

rows.name: Pietra dura workshops
rows.desc: Agra workshops cut coloured stones into marble for the Taj and palaces.

rows.name: Imperial karkhanas of Delhi
rows.desc: Bernier described royal workshops in the fort where embroiderers, goldsmiths and painters worked.

rows.name: Alamgirnama
rows.desc: Muhammad Kazim wrote the official history of Aurangzeb's first ten years.
